dedupe_keys.name: sahana eden open source application kit for emergency and humanitarian management

description: Sahana EDEN is an open-source rapid application development kit for building web-based, database-driven information systems for emergency and humanitarian management. It is maintained by the Sahana Software Foundation with a community of implementing organisations and support teams in Germany, Sweden and Poland; since May 2025 the Eden ASP code base is the main branch and the earlier EDEN code is archived as EDEN Legacy. Coverage: generic software, deployed by aid organisations and government agencies in many countries for preparedness, response and recovery. The kit provides multi-tenant, multi-role modules for organisations, people, case management of individual beneficiaries (for example the refugee case management template MRCMS), shelters, requests, inventory and assets, projects and mapping, configured through templates; the foundation also offers related tools for common alerting protocol messaging and incident management. Format and access: Python application on the web2py framework, source on GitHub with a developer handbook on ReadTheDocs and a wiki; free. Licence: MIT. Caveats: it is a toolkit for developers and service providers, not a ready product, each deployment holds its own data, and older EDEN Legacy templates are no longer developed. Simulation uses: an operational data layer for shelters, stocks and people in emergency response exercises and digital twin set-ups of humanitarian logistics. Related records: Resgrid (platform-resgrid-computer-aided-dispatch) covers dispatch for responders, and IFRC GO (data-ifrc-go-emergency-operations-api) is a humanitarian operations platform with public data.
